Customers subscribe on an out-of-stock product through the Store API POST /api/v3/store/products/:product_id/back_in_stock_subscriptions (guest-accessible, rate-limited; body {email}, normalized/downcased; find_or_initialize_by(product,email) re-activates a previously-notified subscription; 404 when product missing). Email delivery uses the store's configured SMTP (Resend: smtp.resend.com / SMTP_USERNAME=resend / SMTP_PASSWORD=re_... in server .env only). Admin lists/deletes subscriptions at /admin/back_in_stock_subscriptions (settings nav, table with product/email/status/created_at).

scenarios.description: After rolling back to 2155920 (no order-split/combined-payment), three regressions resurfaced: (1) the PDP crashed with `TypeError: b?.toFixed is not a function` because ProductReviews rendered `averageRating?.toFixed(1)` while the Store API serializes average_rating as a string (BigDecimal) — fixed by wrapping in Number(). scenarios.description: FIN-P4-8（PRD-20260906-payments-fin-p4-8）：运维闭环收官。FinancialLedger::RepairTransaction（Journal 幂等补记 §49）：枚举 txn 可达 payments/refunds/splits 按 journal-missing 分区（already_present vs 缺失），修复委托 PostPayment/PostRefund/PostAllocation 幂等原语；绝不重新 Payment/Refund/改 state/自动 charge（INV-08/09）。Reconciliations::ReconcileSweeperJob（sidekiq-cron 保守自动，参考 RecoverSweeperJob）：扫描 completed/payment_confirmed/finalizing → 逐个 ReconcileTransaction（只读）统计 status_counts（event=reconciliations.sweeper metrics）；journal-missing 自动 enqueue RepairTransactionJob（幂等安全 §44）；mismatch/needs_attention/pending 绝不自动动资金，仅 warn（§46 人工）。reconciliations.rake：list_needs_attention/reconcile[txn]/repair[txn]/backfill[store]。Backfill 三类（§50/AC-4025）：PROVABLE→补 journal；PARTIALLY_PROVABLE→只补本地+PENDING/UNSUPPORTED 如实；UNPROVABLE→不写不猜保留 legacy。无 migration（legacy 处置沿用既有 journal/UNSUPPORTED 语义）；admin UI/timeline/audit 目录范围外；全量 backend-rspec 0 failures
mustDo: RepairTransaction 幂等补记：captured payment 缺 CASH_CAPTURED / succeeded refund 缺 REFUND_SUCCEEDED / settled combination splits 缺 ORDER_ALLOCATION → 补记（委托既有幂等原语）
repair 绝不重新 Payment/Refund/改任何 state machine/自动 charge（INV-08/09/12，唯一写 = Journal）
repair 幂等：重复运行不重复 entry；already_present 统计正确；不可证明源（无 provider reference 等）不修不猜
ReconcileSweeperJob 保守自动：journal-missing → 自动 enqueue RepairTransactionJob；mismatch/needs_attention → 仅 warn 不自动动资金（§44/§46）
sweeper 输出结构化 metrics（event/reconciliations.sweeper/store_id/status_counts/needs_human）；重复运行无副作用
rake list_needs_attention/reconcile/repair/backfill 存在且可执行
backfill 三类：PROVABLE 补 journal；PARTIALLY 只补本地 + PENDING/UNSUPPORTED 如实；UNPROVABLE 不写不猜（AC-4025）
全链路只读/幂等：零自动 charge/refund、零新 Payment/Refund、零 transaction state 倒退
mustNotDo: repair/sweeper/backfill 触发重新 Payment/Refund/charge 或倒退 transaction state（INV-08/09 必须禁止）
sweeper 对 mismatch/needs_attention/provider 冲突自动动资金（§46 必须人工，仅 journal-missing 自动）
refund 无 provider reference 等不可证明源被 repair（必须不修不猜）
backfill UNPROVABLE 猜 captured/ownership/currency 或写半套事实（AC-4025/§50 必须保留 legacy）
在 FIN-P4-8 做 Admin Financial View UI / Financial Timeline / finance.* audit 目录（范围外）或加 migration
repair 绕过既有幂等 Post 原语直接 create entry（必须委托 PostPayment/PostRefund/PostAllocation）

scenarios.name: REV-P6-1 Durable Refund Lifecycle：Refund = durable execution aggregate（requested→processing→succeeded/failed/ambiguous），闭合 orphan PSP refund
scenarios.description: REV-P6-1（PRD-20260906-payments-rev-p6-1-durable-refund-lifecycle-foundation）：Refund 由 successful-refund-only row 升级为带状态机（requested/processing/succeeded/failed/ambiguous/manual_review/canceled）的 Durable Refund Execution Aggregate；删除 after_create :perform!「create 即 PSP 副作用」；新增 Refunds::Execute（claim 锁内重校验 capacity→provider I/O→三态持久化，ApplySuccess 独立可重放）；Payment#refundable_capacity = amount − succeeded − active(requested/processing/ambiguous)，failed/canceled 释放；仅 refund.succeeded → PostRefund（REFUND_SUCCEEDED）；历史 backfill state=succeeded（transaction_id 存在）不猜 ownership。
mustDo: 任何 PSP refund 副作用前本地必有 durable Refund row（AC-6001）；Refund 创建失败不得调用 PSP（AC-6002）

requested/processing/ambiguous 占用 refundable capacity（AC-6007/6008）；FAILED 释放（AC-6009）；并发 partial refund 不超付
timeout/未知结果 → ambiguous，不自动创建第二笔 Refund（AC-6005）；明确拒绝 → failed durable 留痕（不 raise 回滚）
PSP success + 本地投影失败 → durable row 保持 processing/ambiguous（可 ApplySuccess 重放，AC-6006 底座）
仅 SUCCEEDED 触发 REFUND_SUCCEEDED journal posting（AC-6013/6014）；非 succeeded 不误入账
P0-P5 baseline 全绿（AC-6030~6035）；新增 lifecycle/capacity/execute spec + 受影响 refund/gateway/reimbursement/P4 posting spec 全绿
mustNotDo: 保留 after_create :perform! / create 内同步 PSP（REV-INV-03 反例）
ambiguous 结果自动重退或猜 FAILED 再退一次（REV-INV-04/16）
failed/canceled/requested 退款减少 payment_total 或产生 REFUND_SUCCEEDED ledger entry
Refund 失败 raise 回滚丢弃 durable 记录（无本地 owner 的 orphan PSP refund）
回退 CommerceTransaction/Payment 或建 ReverseTransaction/第二套 Refund ownership

scenarios.description: REV-P6-2（PRD-20260906-payments-rev-p6-2-refund-execution-orchestration）：退款发起与资金执行解耦——Refunds::Request（capacity 校验 → durable requested → enqueue ExecuteJob）为唯一发起入口；ExecuteJob（Sidekiq）async 执行 Refunds::Execute；Admin refunds#create 与 Stripe/Adyen/PayPal gateway cancel 自动退款改为 async（201 state=requested / 立即成功，退款后台执行）；reimbursement 退货链本包保留同步（REV-P6-5）；Recover/Sweeper 归 REV-P6-6。
mustDo: 任何 PSP 副作用前 durable requested 已落库，且只由 ExecuteJob 调 Refunds::Execute（生产无 request/业务事务内同步 PSP 退款路径）
ExecuteJob 幂等：终态（processing/succeeded/failed/ambiguous/manual_review/canceled）不重复执行；重试不产生第二笔 PSP 退款

gateway cancel（completed）登记 durable 退款请求并立即成功，不再链内同步 PSP / 不回滚取消链

mustNotDo: 在 Admin/取消/业务事务内同步 gateway.credit（REV-INV-03）

scenarios.name: Pull-deploy decides on the running state, not on a state file

scenarios.name: Dispute operations report stays read-only and degrades instead of guessing
scenarios.description: DSP-P7-10 B2 (FR-006): a store-scoped, read-only disputes report behind the admin list page — win rate, reason-code breakdown, deadline achievement and handling time, with explicit degradation for mixed currencies and failures

scenarios.name: Evidence drafts need a second operator before the provider is called

scenarios.name: Dispute deadline alerts remind and escalate without automating anything
scenarios.description: DSP-P7-10 B2 (FR-007): a subscriber turns the sweeper's due-soon / overdue events into audit trail, metrics and an operator-facing escalation flag, while the scanner itself stays read-only

mustNotDo: Automate submission, acceptance, refunds, restock or re-billing from a reminder event

scenarios.name: Evidence receipt state moves forward only and is never guessed
scenarios.description: DSP-P7-10 B3 (FR-009): the submitted → acknowledged → rejected receipt state is derived from provider write-backs instead of mutating the append-only receipt, and degrades to unknown when signals conflict

Write rows, publish events or call the provider from the state derivation

scenarios.name: Handling a dispute never moves stock by itself

scenarios.name: Checkout post-submit errors route by code, not by the presence of an order id
scenarios.description: PRD-20260913-checkout-txn-error-routing: the single-page checkout must branch on the server error code — quote changes return to the order page for re-confirmation, stock failures stay in page, paid-but-recovering transactions are shown as received without any retry entry, and unknown codes keep the legacy result-page fallback (RESEARCH-20260913 §9.2)

Keep INSUFFICIENT_STOCK / INVENTORY_CHANGED / RESERVATION_EXPIRED in page with a role=alert notice and a return-to-cart CTA, never stating 'payment failed' and never jumping to the result page

scenarios.name: Money uses raw fields for logic and display strings only for rendering
scenarios.description: PRD-20260913-checkout-money-contract: conditional rendering must use the raw amount fields (delivery_total / tax_total / discount_total); display_* strings carry currency symbols and must never be parsed — and TOTAL SAVINGS counts promotion discounts only (RESEARCH-20260913 §9.1 P0-a)
mustDo: Judge row visibility from the raw amount fields (safeParseFloat) and keep display_* strictly for rendering

scenarios.name: Billing intent is modelled server-side and the order snapshot always has a billing address
scenarios.description: PRD-20260913-checkout-billing-mode: the storefront sends billing_mode (same_as_shipping | custom) instead of the legacy use_shipping flag, choosing same-as-shipping clears the cart billing address, and Carts::Submit snapshots an explicit billing address first and falls back to the shipping address (RESEARCH-20260913 §9.1 P0-b)

scenarios.name: Cart discount codes resolve for canonical carts and are redeemed (or refused) at submit

scenarios.name: Prefixed ids are ownership-checked so one resource's id can never resolve as another's
scenarios.description: PRD-20260914-other-prefixedid-ownership-validation (research §9.1 P0-f): the prefixed-id decoder used to discard the prefix and look up the decoded integer directly, so an `or_...` order id could resolve as a product/variant sharing that PK; the prefix is now enforced to be the calling class's own has_prefix_id declaration (RESEARCH-20260913 §9.1 P0-f)

scenarios.name: Checkout placeholders are either wired or hidden — never fake controls

scenarios.name: Canonical cart gift cards resolve on cart_ ids and stay money-free until submit

scenarios.description: PRD-20260914-checkout B1: the or_ pay page must render gift-card/store-credit rows, the payment-method list and edit/pay gating from the server CheckoutView projection instead of inferring them from the Order snapshot; the fields stay read-only and additive so an older payload still renders

scenarios.name: Cart-stage credits are intent only — the cart page shows what was asked for, not money moved
scenarios.description: PRD-20260914-checkout B2: the canonical cart page gains a discounts/credits module (coupon, gift card, store credit) and a three-row summary, all fed by the server ShoppingCart intent snapshot; nothing is redeemed until carts.submit, and store credit stays login-gated and mutually exclusive with gift cards

Leave the credit intent fields untyped (unknown) in the generated/hand-written types so the storefront has to assert its way into them

scenarios.name: Inventory errors keep their own landing spots and the result page shows fulfilment without trace ids
scenarios.description: PRD-20260915-checkout B3: the three stock codes (INSUFFICIENT_STOCK / INVENTORY_CHANGED / RESERVATION_EXPIRED) each need their own copy and action, an expired reservation may auto-retry exactly once, INVENTORY_RECOVERY_REQUIRED must never invite a second payment, and the payment result page must show fulfilment information (including shipment groups) without leaking transaction/reservation/payment-session identifiers

mustNotDo: Deprecate-mark canonical cart_ traffic that shares the same route shape, or count it as legacy traffic

scenarios.name: Admin theming goes through brand tokens and a density switch, never through component hard-codes
scenarios.description: PRD-20260915-admin B6-1: the Rails admin must expose brand colour scales, semantic tokens and a two-step density switch from a single theme file, keep components free of direct Tailwind palette usage on primary semantics, ship a machine-checked token/contrast contract, and let hosts override the look from their own Tailwind entry point

scenarios.name: Checkout stays single-page, but the server contract is two-stage: prepare the order quote, then pay against it

The combined cart_id form stays for wallet express, and the prepared order is remembered so retries never re-submit the cart.

scenarios.name: Payment providers are configured per method (option), not per provider
scenarios.description: PRD-20260915-admin 支付配置选项化 (D1 slices 1-3): one payment provider record can expose several storefront entries (methods). Entries live in metadata (optionized + options[]) until the dedicated table lands; the admin edits them on the provider edit page (catalog table + Test connection + masked credentials), and the gateway-side contract (collect_frontend_payment_methods / PaymentSessions::Start) reads the same source so a disabled option can never be offered and then rejected at payment time.
mustDo: Keep the entry API behind the payment_option* prefix (Gateway#options already exists on gateway providers) and read/write metadata['options'] with kind/active/position/frontend_kind/display_name only

Treat optionized as the migration gate: absent means one implicit default entry (legacy behaviour unchanged); true means exactly the enabled options, and zero enabled options means zero storefront entries

Normalize on write: only kinds from the provider capability catalog (payment_option_catalog) are accepted, any enabled option flips optionized to true, and existing kinds missing from the submitted form are preserved
Run Test connection through PallasTrade::PaymentMethods::TestConnection, persist {ok, code, message, checked_at} into metadata['last_test_connection'] and audit the action
Mask :password typed preferences everywhere (page and API return only the masked last-4 value; provider error messages are sanitized before they are stored or logged)
mustNotDo: Overwrite or shadow Gateway#options, or store option state anywhere except metadata['options']/['optionized']
Flip optionized from a save that enabled nothing (a name-only or display_on-only edit must not silently empty the storefront list)
Let an option kind outside the catalog reach metadata, or drop configured kinds that the admin form did not render
Trigger provider validations (network calls) just to persist a Test connection result, or let a credential value reach a log/message/report

scenarios.name: PDP availability states stay truthful and the SKU is deep-linkable
scenarios.description: PRD-20260915-catalog-pdp-state-correctness (Batch A of the catalog upgrade plan): the PDP derives its presentation state from Store API flags only (in_stock > preorder > backorder > out_of_stock) so pre-order / backorder SKUs stay purchasable instead of being rendered as sold out with a back-in-stock form; `?variant=` becomes the shareable SKU deep link (server-seeded initial selection, router.replace on switch, unknown ids fall back); and buildProductJsonLd emits AggregateOffer price ranges plus a metafield-sourced brand.
mustDo: Derive the availability presentation state from existing Store API flags (in_stock/purchasable/preorder/backorderable) via the pure helpers in lib/utils/variant-selection.ts — in stock > pre-order > backorder > sold out, and pre-order/backorder only while the SKU is purchasable
Keep pre-order/backorder SKUs purchasable (Add to Cart + Buy Now enabled, no BackInStockNotify) and show the localized ship-by date when preorder_ships_at is present

Treat `?variant=` as the canonical deep link: page.tsx reads searchParams.variant into initialVariantId, an unknown/stale id falls back to default_variant → first purchasable → first, and switching SKUs updates the URL with router.replace(..., { scroll: false }) while preserving other query params

Report GA4 view_item with the variant the page was opened with (trackViewItem(product, currency, initialVariant)) and keep canonical/OG metadata on the product URL (no per-SKU SEO pages in this batch)

Emit AggregateOffer (lowPrice/highPrice/offerCount/priceCurrency + most favourable availability) for multi-SKU products, keep a plain Offer for single SKU, and read brand from a custom field (catalog.brand / brand / *.brand) with the field omitted when absent
mustNotDo: Render the back-in-stock form for a SKU that can actually be bought (pre-order / backorder), or show the pre-order badge for a SKU whose oversell allowance ran out (that is sold out)
Bypass the pure helpers with inline flag juggling in the component, or invent availability/price fields the serializers do not send
Push a new history entry on variant switch, drop existing query params (e.g. category_id), or error on an unknown variant id
Re-fire view_item on every variant switch, or change PRODUCT_PAGE_EXPAND / add new Store API requests for this feature
Ship new user-facing strings without the five message files (de/en/es/fr/pl) and the products i18n guard, or let brand leak into the schema when no custom field exists

scenarios.name: Admin bulk operations preview first, then apply through one code path
scenarios.description: PRD-20260915-admin-bulk-operations-2 (Batch B-1 of the catalog upgrade plan): the products table gains five preview-first bulk actions (set price / adjust price % / adjust inventory / add channel / remove channel) on top of the existing add_bulk_action framework — each action renders a modal form, a dry-run preview that writes nothing, and an apply step that reuses the same service so preview and apply counts agree.
mustDo: Keep the domain logic in pallastrade_core services (Products::BulkPriceUpdate / BulkInventoryAdjust / BulkChannelAssignment) whose preview and apply share one `run(dry_run:)` and return a Result struct with selected/updated/skipped counts plus warnings

Write prices only to base prices in the selected currency (Price.currency upcased): update amount (+ PriceHistory) when the row exists, create it when missing, leave price-list entries untouched, and round percentage adjustments with (amount * factor).round(2)
Clamp inventory at zero, skip untracked items (inventory_not_tracked) and zero deltas (zero_delta), and require a stock location (stock_location_missing) before touching StockItem counts
Assign channels through ProductPublication with add/remove modes, counting already-published pairs on remove instead of failing

Register each action via add_bulk_action with a `condition` guard (can? :manage on Price/StockItem/ProductPublication) and a `*_preview` PUT route that answers with a turbo_stream replacing #bulk_dialog, so the confirm form posts to the apply route
Collect per-record refusals (permission_denied, no_price, negative_result, above_maximum, clamped_at_zero, not_published…) as warnings, apply to the rest, and flash a localized result message
Ship the admin.bulk_ops.products.* keys for every action/form/preview/result/warning and cover the flow with the registered `admin-products-bulk-rspec` verifier
mustNotDo: Let the preview step write anything (no price rows, no StockItem counts, no publications) or compute its counts differently from the apply step
Abort the whole batch when one record is not permitted or not applicable — that record is skipped with a warning while the rest proceed
Downcase the currency when looking up/creating a Price, or widen the change beyond base prices into price lists
Route the apply step through a second implementation that can drift from the previewed counts
Assert admin engine translations with a raw I18n lookup (the environment misses them, including pre-existing keys) instead of PallasTrade.t, or render a modal form without its i18n keys

scenarios.name: Payment availability scope evaluated by one shared resolver
scenarios.description: PRD-20260915-payments-d8 (D8 first slice): a payment option (kind) can be scoped by market / country / zone / currency through an entry-level `rule_set` stored in the payment method metadata — the storefront list, the admin back-end list and `PaymentSessions::Start` must all evaluate it through the same `PallasTrade::Payments::Availability::Resolver`, and the admin payment-method tab gains a scope editor plus a human summary.
mustDo: Store the rule set as additive JSON: `metadata['options'][i]['rule_set'] = { match: 'all'|'any', include: [ { dimension, operator, values } ], exclude: [...] }` with dimensions market/country/zone/currency and operators in/not_in/eq — normalized on read and write (market/zone raw ids, country/currency uppercase ISO, invalid dimensions/operators/blank values dropped, both sides empty => nil = available everywhere)

Evaluate through `Availability::RuleSet` + `Context` + `Evaluator` + `Resolver`: exclude wins over include, `match: any` needs one include hit, unresolvable observed values never match, and the resolver additionally narrows by provider scope (frontend/back_end) and the provider capability catalog (declared currencies/countries)
Route every consumer through the resolver — `Order#payment_methods`, `collect_frontend_payment_methods`, `collect_backend_payment_methods` — so no caller re-implements the rule semantics

Re-check the requested option inside `PaymentSessions::Start` (option kind -> available options) and fail with `payment_option_not_available` without creating a session when the option is out of scope

Expose the scope in the admin API as `options[].rule_set` (normalized) plus `options[].scope_summary` (i18n dimension names), and refresh generated contracts via `scripts/ci/contracts.sh` instead of hand-editing SDK types

Accept prefix ids in the admin form (`mkt_`/`zone_`) but persist raw ids, validating markets against the provider store and countries/currencies against real ISO data plus the store supported-currency list
Cover the behaviour with the registered `d8-availability-rspec` verifier (resolver + order projection + start gate + admin scope editing)
mustNotDo: Let the storefront list, the admin list and Start compute availability from different code paths (that is the 'selectable but unpayable' failure mode)
Treat an unknown context as available through the include branch (or unavailable through the exclude branch) — observed values that cannot be resolved must not match
Persist prefix ids, lowercase ISO codes or capability-unknown dimensions into the rule set, or keep a rule when every submitted value was dropped (empty scope = 不限)
Drop pre-existing `exclude` conditions when the admin form only manages include conditions
Change behaviour for providers without a rule set, non-optionized providers or stores without markets (zero-regression behaviour must stay identical)

scenarios.name: Catalog Health turns scattered catalog gaps into an actionable worklist
scenarios.description: PRD-20260915-admin-catalog-health-v1 (Batch B-2 of the catalog upgrade plan): Products gains a Catalog Health page that reports seven actionable issues (missing media / description / SEO / translations, active + zero stock, unresolved redirects, old drafts) with a drill-down per count — the five product-level issues reuse the very scopes the counts were computed with, so the filtered products list always matches the number that was clicked, and the merchant can continue into the bulk operations built in Batch B-1.
mustDo: Keep one source of truth for the seven issues (PallasTrade::CatalogHealth::Issues) and let both the worklist page and the products-list filter resolve through it, so a count equals the length of the filtered list
Count missing media from pallastrade_assets across the product and its variants (master included) — Asset declares no counter cache, so the rows are the truth
Compare description/SEO against the effective default-locale value (Mobility translation row first, model column as fallback), and flag SEO when either meta_title or meta_description is missing

Treat an active product as zero-stock only when no variant is sellable: track_inventory = false, preorderable, a stock item with count_on_hand > 0 or backorderable — pre-order and backorder SKUs stay out of the report

Reuse the existing surfaces for remediation: missing translations links to the Product Translations coverage page (same `name` rule), unresolved redirects links to the URL-changes section of the Redirects page (ProductUrlChange handled: false)

Filter the products list by overriding `scope` behind a validated `health_issue` param, render the filter banner through the `products_header_partials` injection point, and register the sidebar entry under Products guarded by can?(:read, PallasTrade::Product)

Keep the page read-only and 200 on failure: each counter degrades to 0 with a logged warning instead of taking the worklist down, and sync the navigation consistency spec whenever a Products sub-item is added
mustNotDo: Compute counts and filters with two different definitions (they drift and the drill-down shows a different number than the badge)
Rely on media_count counters or instance-only helpers (has_media?) for the missing-media scope, or count archived products
Report pre-order/backorderable or untracked-inventory products as out of stock, or count drafts as sellable
Invent a new locale rule for translations instead of the one the Product Translations page already applies
Add write paths (no create/update/destroy, no one-click fixes) on the health page, or copy gem views to the host app instead of using the documented injection point

scenarios.name: PDP turns into a discovery node without inventing backend surface
scenarios.description: PRD-20260915-catalog-batch-c1-discovery (Batch C-1 of the catalog upgrade plan): the product page gains three discovery rails — rule-based related products (same categories, buyable, never the product on screen), a browser-local recently-viewed rail and a browser-local wishlist with its own page and header entry. No recommendation algorithm, no server-side domain model: the catalog filters already shipped by the Store API carry related, while the two personal rails live entirely in localStorage and degrade silently when storage is unavailable.
mustDo: Derive related products from the existing list endpoint (`in_categories` + `in_stock`, over-fetching one row) and drop the product on screen before trimming to the limit, so the rail never shows a duplicate or an out-of-stock item
Hide the related rail entirely (heading included) when the product has no categories or nothing matches, and keep it on the cached list fetch so it shares the `products` cache tag
Keep recently viewed browser-local: newest first, one entry per product (a repeat visit moves to the front), capped at 12, and never suggesting the product being viewed

Keep the wishlist V1 browser-local too: toggle on the product page, count badge in the header, `/wishlist` page with removal and an empty state that leads back to the catalog — no server model, no new endpoint

Keep the product-page wishlist toggle a lightweight secondary action (`outline` + `sm`) on the availability row, so quantity + Add to Cart + Buy Now always own the primary action row instead of being squeezed by a full-width `lg` button

Push the list arithmetic into pure modules (related-products / recently-viewed / wishlist) and route every storage access through one try/catch helper, so private mode or a full quota degrades to "not persisted" instead of breaking the page
Read browser state only after mount (first paint renders nothing / zero) and sync rails through same-page events plus cross-tab `storage` events, keeping hydration deterministic
Ship every new string in the five message files and register the keys in the i18n guard test, reusing ProductCard's analytics rather than adding new tracking code
mustNotDo: Introduce a recommendation algorithm, a tags-based fallback or a similarity service in V1 — the plan explicitly defers that until real exposure/click data exists
Create a server-side wishlist/recently-viewed model, migration or API endpoint, or a new SDK method
Read localStorage during render (hydration mismatch, empty-state flash) or let a corrupt payload throw instead of degrading to an empty list
Show the rail for out-of-stock matches, show the current product in its own rails, or render an empty section with a heading
Hardcode colours or bypass the design tokens/Tailwind conventions when building the rails, or add a user-facing string without the five-language guard entry

scenarios.name: Back-in-stock subscriptions become SKU-aware without double-notifying anyone
scenarios.description: PRD-20260915-catalog-batch-c2-sku-back-in-stock (§9 of the catalog upgrade plan): back-in-stock subscriptions gain an optional variant dimension. StockMovement::CustomEvents publishes variant.back_in_stock when one SKU becomes buyable again, the subscriber routes that event only to that SKU's subscribers while the product-level event keeps serving the historical variant_id IS NULL rows, the Store API accepts an optional variant_id, and the admin list shows the SKU.
mustDo: Keep variant_id nullable on pallastrade_back_in_stock_subscriptions and encode both semantics with two partial unique indexes: (product_id, variant_id, email) WHERE variant_id IS NOT NULL and (product_id, email) WHERE variant_id IS NULL — Postgres does not de-duplicate NULLs, so a single three-column index would let legacy rows duplicate
Validate in the model that a subscription's variant belongs to its product, scope the email uniqueness by variant_id, and expose for_variant/product_level scopes for the notification split

Publish variant.back_in_stock from StockMovement::CustomEvents when the variant transitions from unbuyable to buyable, carrying the variant's prefixed id in the payload, and leave product.out_of_stock/product.back_in_stock semantics untouched

Route variant.back_in_stock only to that variant's active subscriptions and product.back_in_stock only to the legacy product-level rows, so nobody is emailed twice and SKU subscribers never get another SKU's restock

Accept an optional variant_id on POST /api/v3/store/products/:product_id/back_in_stock_subscriptions (prefixed or integer, must belong to the product → otherwise 404), return variant_id in the response, and regenerate the OpenAPI/SDK contracts
Subscribe from the product page with the selected variant, and show the SKU in the admin subscriptions table (product-level rows stay readable as —)
Mark a subscription notified right after the email is queued and keep it active when delivery raises, so a failure stays retryable
mustNotDo: Replace the legacy product-level uniqueness rule or make variant_id NOT NULL (historical rows must keep working)
Notify SKU subscribers from the product-level event (or the reverse) — that reintroduces either the wrong-SKU email or a duplicate email
Match a variant id without checking it belongs to the product in the path, or return a 201 for a variant from another product
Send a raw integer primary key in the API response instead of the prefixed variant id
Hand-edit generated contracts (OpenAPI schemas / SDK types) instead of regenerating them, or ship the API change without generated:check staying green

scenarios.name: Product history timeline reuses audit logs instead of a new history table
scenarios.description: PRD-20260915-catalog-batch-d1-product-history (§12 step 2 of the catalog upgrade plan): the admin product edit page shows a timeline of field changes, batch operations and price changes. Writes go through PallasTrade::ProductHistory::Recorder on top of pallastrade_audit_logs (zero migrations), reads through PallasTrade::ProductHistory::Timeline, and the panel is injected via the product form sidebar partials without overriding the gem form.
mustDo: Persist history in pallastrade_audit_logs (resource_type 'PallasTrade::Product') instead of adding a product_history table, and keep the tracked attribute set explicit (name/slug/status/description/meta_title/meta_description/available_on/discontinue_on)
Snapshot the product before the update and record after success, skipping the entry when nothing changed and no nested-section context exists, so no-op saves do not pollute the timeline

Record batch operations (bulk price/inventory/channel/status) as one entry per affected product with metadata['source']='bulk' plus updated_count/skipped_count, and normalise the actor to {type,id,label} with a 'system' fallback
Annotate nested form sections (variants/media/categories) in metadata['sections'] instead of pretending they are columns, and render them as a section summary

Merge audit entries with PriceHistory in Timeline.call (descending occurred_at, capped by limit) and derive a price entry's previous amount from the next older row of the same price record, carrying variant_sku/variant_id in metadata
Inject the panel through the product form sidebar partials with admin.product_history.* translations, so the gem product form stays untouched
Scope the timeline to the product passed in (never a global audit scan), and make PUT/PATCH updates and batch actions both write through the recorder
mustNotDo: Add a new history table or migration when the audit log already stores before/after snapshots
Write an entry for a save that changed nothing, or record every tracked attribute on update instead of just the diff
Leave the actor unlabelled or store a raw actor object — the panel shows a human label or 'system'
Copy the gem product form into the host app to add the panel (AP-008) instead of using the partial injection point
Hand-roll a second price-change reader that disagrees with PriceHistory, or show a price change without the previous amount

scenarios.name: Duplicate products surface as candidates instead of silent clones
scenarios.description: PRD-20260915-catalog-batch-d2-duplicate-detection (§12 step 3 of the catalog upgrade plan): the catalog has no duplicate protection at all — SKU validation can be disabled and allows blanks, barcode has a column and an index but no validation whatsoever, and product names are unconstrained. PallasTrade::Products::DuplicateCandidates groups the store's products by normalized barcode / SKU / name and the admin worklist shows those groups with a side-by-side comparison. Detection only: merging is a separate project (D-3).
mustDo: Keep the detection semantics in one place (Products::DuplicateCandidates) so the worklist counts and the candidate rows are derived from the same groups — a count can never disagree with the list underneath it
Group by LOWER(TRIM(...)) on the variant barcode, the variant SKU and the product name, and only keep groups spanning more than one product (HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT products.id) > 1)
Scope every query to the current store, exclude soft-deleted products/variants and archived products, and remember that variants have no store column — the store comes from the product join

Drop blank group keys by filtering the grouped keys, never with where.not(col: [nil, '']) — that renders NOT (col = NULL OR col IS NULL), which is NULL and therefore never true for real rows (and is cast unexpectedly on Mobility-translated attributes)
Build the aggregate SQL from Arel nodes (NamedFunction / count(distinct:)) instead of interpolated strings, so the page never reintroduces a SQL-injection finding

Present a read-only worklist (signal counts, filtered candidate groups, +N more) plus a comparison view with the fields a merchant needs to decide, and wire it into the Products submenu with the product read permission
Say plainly in the UI and the docs that these are candidates: detection never merges, renames or archives anything
mustNotDo: Treat duplicate slugs as a signal — Product::Slugs appends a uuid on conflict, so the duplicates are invisible there
Return every candidate row unbounded or group variants of the same product into phantom candidates (a group counts products, not rows)
Let another store's SKU/barcode/name leak into a group, or ignore soft-deleted variants
Ship a merge/auto-fix action in the same slice — merging has to reconcile variants, reviews, redirects and historical transactions
Add a migration or an API contract change for a read-only worklist

scenarios.name: Frontend payment keys are delivered by the API instead of being baked into the build
scenarios.description: PRD-20260915-payments-d10-client-config (D10 of the payments batch plan, §68.4/§76.1): the server now ships `client_config` on every payment-method payload (checkout `payment.available_payment_methods[]` plus the store `PaymentMethodSerializer` used by cart/order), exposing only publishable-level credentials, so switching payment provider or test/live environment is a back-office change instead of a redeploy + image rebuild; the storefront reads the API value first and keeps a temporary fallback to NEXT_PUBLIC_* while everything turns green.
mustDo: Assemble client_config in exactly one place (PallasTrade::PaymentMethods::ClientConfig) as { provider, environment, publishable, session_token } and reuse it from both the checkout serializer and the store PaymentMethodSerializer

Derive publishable keys from the provider's declared public_preference_keys (symbols — preferences are stored with symbol keys) and reuse the D9 credential levels so secret/internal values can never be projected
Resolve env: references at read time (missing ENV omits the key instead of raising or leaking the reference string), and keep the contract additive so older clients keep rendering
Let the Stripe gateway declare [:publishable_key] as public while secret_key stays a :password preference, and keep the 'no secrets through public preferences' regression assertion green
Regenerate the contract with scripts/ci/contracts.sh (OpenAPI + SDK/zod types) and keep generated:check at zero drift, including the checkout typelize fields that had drifted from the payload

Make the storefront dual-read: resolveStripePublishableKey(client_config) → NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY → null, cache loadStripe per key, and thread client_config from the selected payment method into CardPaymentForm / StripePaymentForm / ExpressCheckoutButton
mustNotDo: Ship secret or internal credentials to the browser, or invent a second credential-projection path next to the D9 level/Gateways declarations
Store the resolved plaintext back into preferences, or read publishable keys with string keys (they silently resolve to nil)
Keep a module-level stripePromise singleton, or hard-fail the card form when client_config is absent (the fallback must keep the old behaviour)
Edit generated SDK/OpenAPI outputs by hand instead of regenerating them from the serializers

scenarios.name: AI drafts product copy but never saves it
scenarios.description: PRD-20260915-catalog-batch-e1-ai-copilot (§7 and §15 of the catalog upgrade plan): the AI engine already ships a gateway, a capability registry, run/artifact audit and its availability gates — what was missing was the wiring. Two capabilities (catalog.product_description, catalog.product_seo) now feed the product edit page, where the merchant gets a preview and must Accept before anything reaches the form. Saving stays a separate human action.
mustDo: Register the product capabilities in code for every environment (not in the dev/test-only registry), declare execution :sync, data classification internal and the product update authorization on the capability itself
Assemble prompts in a business service that reads the product facts and calls PallasTrade::AI::Gateway, and keep the handler classes contract-compatible without duplicating prompt logic
Keep the run audit: every generation creates a PallasTrade::AI::Run with the actor, capability, model and usage, and only the input digest is persisted (never the prompt or the response body)
Return the draft to the admin and require an explicit Accept before the textarea/meta fields change — the endpoint itself must not write the product, and saving remains the merchant's own action
Check availability before use (side-effect free) so an unconfigured store renders disabled buttons with the reason, and answer failures with a stable error code the UI can translate
Keep the admin engine free of a hard dependency on the AI engine: no AI installed means the product form renders exactly as before
mustNotDo: Auto-save AI output, auto-fill the form without consent, or touch price, inventory, channel or publish state
Bypass the gateway (direct provider calls) or the availability gates, or build a second prompt layer inside the handler
Persist prompt text, provider payloads or credentials in the run records or the response
Let another store's product be drafted by passing its id, or leak another store's catalog facts into a prompt
Ship the assistant as a hard requirement for the admin engine (breaking apps without pallastrade_ai)

scenarios.name: Webhook events become an operable queue instead of a SQL session
scenarios.description: PRD-20260915-payments-d12-webhook-governance (D12, plan §69): every verified provider webhook already lands as a durable PaymentWebhookEvent, but nothing could see it. D12 turns it into a console under Developers -> Webhook events: filter the stream (provider / action / status / order number / date), open a row for the raw payload and the handler outcome, then replay it through the original chain, quarantine unknown types (kept for the record, never processed), or mark it processed when it was already handled out of band - plus 24h inbound/outbound health and a subscription checklist that flags actions never received.
mustDo: Keep the existing reliability envelope intact: quarantine is a status on the event shell (quarantined_at + quarantine_reason) that blocks replay, and unknown exceptions still have to raise so the job retries

Route every action through a small service that writes an Audit entry with the acting admin (replay stays on Payments::ReplayWebhookEvent, quarantine and mark-processed get their own), so who-did-what is answerable
Put filtering in one model scope (provider / action / status / received_at window / order number via payment_session -> order) and let the controller only validate parameters

Compute health as read-only aggregates over a bounded window (inbound status counts, backlog, failure rate, average processing time; outbound success/failure/backlog) with a single SQL pass per metric

Derive the subscription checklist from the provider declaration (PaymentMethod#webhook_event_subscriptions -> #webhook_expected_actions) versus observed actions in the last 30 days, surfacing both missing (never received) and undeclared events
Register the console the way this repo already does: custom admin controller over model_class for authorization, breadcrumbs, nav entry plus tabs entry, and an updated navigation consistency spec
mustNotDo: Let the console perform business writes (no refunds, captures, order or inventory changes) - it only moves the event shell and records the decision
Allow replay of a quarantined event, or a second handler run while an event is processing
Fold inbound provider events into the outbound WebhookDelivery model, or assume their success semantics are interchangeable
Ship a page that 500s when an aggregate fails, or one that loads every payload to compute statistics
Call the provider from the checklist or the health cards

scenarios.name: AI fills only the missing translations and the merchant still saves
scenarios.description: PRD-20260915-catalog-batch-e2-ai-translate-missing (§7.1 Translation row of the catalog upgrade plan): the product translations drawer already edits one locale at a time (Mobility translation tables, name_<locale> inputs, PUT admin_translation_path). E-2 wires a catalog.product_translation capability into that drawer, so the fields still empty in the current locale get drafted from the store default locale, previewed, and written into the form only when the merchant accepts.
mustDo: Decide 'missing' with fallback: false reads — inside a request Mobility falls back to the store default locale, which would make an empty translation look translated
Keep the scope to product content fields (name, description, meta_title, meta_description): translating slug changes storefront URLs and belongs to the redirects workflow
Translate only the empty fields and never overwrite an existing translation, so a partially translated product keeps its reviewed copy
Skip the provider entirely when nothing is missing (stable no_missing_fields reason, no run, no cost) and validate the target locale against the store's supported locales first
Map the drawer's normalized suffix (name_zh_cn) back to the locale code the store declares (zh-CN) before reading through Mobility
Return the draft for the drawer preview and let the regular drawer form save it: accept writes into the form inputs (syncing the rich-text editor), the endpoint itself writes nothing
mustNotDo: Overwrite translations that already exist, or translate into a locale the store does not offer
Invent a second save path for translations, auto-save the draft, or touch slug, price, stock or publish state
Skip the run audit or persist prompt text, provider payloads or credentials
Break the shared translation row partials or other translatable resources while wiring the product drawer
Make the admin engine hard-depend on the AI engine (no AI installed must render the drawer as before)

scenarios.name: The payment row shows the entry-level name without splitting option ids
scenarios.description: PRD-20260916-payments-d16-payment-method-presentation (slice 1 of 搂78-D16 / 搂76.1 of the payment plan): a provider can expose several payment entries (PaymentOption inside metadata['options']), each with its own display_name, but the storefront payment row could only render the provider name. D16 slice 1 adds an entry-level read model (effective_payment_option / option_display_name / option_identifier) and ships option_id, method_key and display_name through the store payment-method contract, so the checkout payment rows render the entry label while keeping one row per provider.
mustDo: Read the entry that the availability resolver already exposed (effective_payment_options.first) and fall back to the default entry, so the label matches what the shopper can actually pay with
Fall back to the provider name when the entry carries no display_name, and to default_option_kind when it carries no kind, so unoptionized payment methods render exactly as before
Expose method_key as its own field so the frontend branches on the entry kind instead of parsing the option_id string
Keep option_id in the same prefixed_id:kind shape the admin line items use, so front and back office talk about the same entry
Ship the three fields through the serializers and regenerate the contract (typelize types, SDK generated types, store/admin yaml) so drift fails the pipeline
Cover both the backend read model and the storefront row: a method with display_name renders it, a method without it renders the provider name
mustNotDo: Invent presentation fields the option metadata does not hold (no icon, no subtitle, no badge), or repurpose the provider-level description
Change the row cardinality, add per-entry rows, or split express wallets in this slice
Render a raw option_id, concatenate kind and provider name in the frontend, or branch on provider type for the label
Break the optionized availability scope or the credential / client_config projections while touching the serializer
Let the contract drift: editing serializers without regenerating types and yaml

scenarios.name: A flaky provider is softened without touching money
scenarios.description: PRD-20260916-payments-d11-circuit-breaker-health (slice 1 of 搂78-D11 / 搂67.3 of the payment plan): when a payment provider starts failing, the entry should disappear from checkout instead of sending shoppers into a broken flow. D11 slice 1 adds entry-level breaker state in payment method metadata, a provider-level health window, an hourly sweep that soft-disables entries past the failure threshold (and auto-restores expired automatic ones), and a resolver gate shared by the storefront list and payment-session start.
mustDo: Keep soft-disable purely presentational: write only payment method metadata plus an audit entry, never cancel sessions, refund, change orders, stock or ledger rows
Store breaker state per entry for optionized providers and provider-wide otherwise, so the manual action can soften exactly one entry
Keep manual soft-disables sticky until a human re-enables them, and let automatic ones expire on their own cooldown
Use one health-metrics implementation for both the decision and the admin card (attempts, failures, failure rate, average duration, top error codes) over a 24h window
Gate availability in the resolver so the storefront list and PaymentSessions::Start agree about whether an entry can be paid with
Require a reason on the manual soft-disable action and record it in the audit log
mustNotDo: Call the provider or any network API to decide health, or block a request path while measuring it
Auto-restore a manual soft-disable, or let a retried sweep re-open the same entry inside its cooldown
Judge on small samples: below min_samples the entry must stay untouched
Duplicate the failure-rate formula in the view or the resolver instead of the shared metrics service
Let one provider error abort the whole sweep, or let a softened entry still be started through the API

scenarios.name: Catalog health advice never repairs anything by itself
scenarios.description: PRD-20260916-catalog-batch-e3-ai-fix-suggestion (§3.3 of the catalog upgrade plan): the Catalog Health worklist already reports seven issues and the AI copilot already drafts content, but nothing told the merchant what to do first. E-3 adds an AI fix suggestion on the worklist rows and on a product sidebar card — an ordered plan whose steps point only at admin surfaces that exist, with no write path at all.
mustDo: Keep the suggestion read-only: the capability authorizes on read, the endpoint and service have no write path, and the UI deliberately has no Accept step because there is nothing to write into
Reuse the worklist's own numbers (CatalogHealth::Report#count_for) so the advice and the page can never disagree, and decide product-level issues with the very same scopes the worklist counts
Cap and minimise sampling: at most five products of that issue with catalog facts only (name, status, price presence, stock) — never customer, order, cost or supplier data
Whitelist the surfaces a step may send the merchant to, and drop an unknown entry while keeping the step, so a suggestion can never advertise an action the admin does not have
Answer nothing_to_fix (no provider call, no run) when the issue count is zero or the product is healthy, and unknown_issue for a key outside the worklist
Render the advice next to the worklist row and on the product sidebar through the existing partial injection point, leaving the existing drill-down links untouched
mustNotDo: Auto-repair anything, batch-apply changes, or write product, translation, price, stock, channel or publish state
Present the output as a done action (no Accept button, no silent save) or invent surfaces, capabilities or numbers the admin does not have
Sample outside the issue scope or pull sensitive fields (customers, orders, costs, suppliers) into the prompt
Break the worklist for stores without the AI engine, or change the Catalog Health issue definitions and counts
Call the provider when there is nothing to fix, or leave a run behind for a rejected suggestion

scenarios.name: Reconciliation differences become a queue a person can work
scenarios.description: PRD-20260916-payments-d13-reconciliation-cases (slice 1 of 搂78-D13 / 搂70.1 of the payment plan): the P4 reconcilers are read-only and deliberately do not persist anything, so mismatches only reached a log line and a rake command. D13 slice 1 persists them as reconciliation cases with an assignee, notes and a close/reopen lifecycle, syncs them from the hourly sweeper, and exposes a back-office workbench with CSV export.
mustDo: Keep the queue a work queue: syncing and every case action write only case rows and audit entries, never payments, refunds, transactions, the ledger, orders or stock
Feed the queue from the existing read-only reconcilers instead of writing a second reconciliation implementation, and keep the journal-repair branch of the sweeper untouched
Key every case on a deterministic signature of the reason codes so repeated sweeps touch the same case (occurrences/last_seen_at) instead of piling up duplicates
Close cases automatically when the difference disappears or is superseded, but never overwrite a decision a person already made (explained, resolved, dismissed)
Expose difference type and severity from one deterministic mapping shared by the model, the page and the CSV
Require a reason to dismiss, require a body for a note, keep the notes append-only, and write an audit entry for every action
Export exactly what the current filters show, with a row cap and a warning when the cap truncates the file
mustNotDo: Move money or change payment/refund/order state from the queue, or call the provider from a case action
Auto-reopen a case a human dismissed, or auto-close one that a human is still investigating without recording why
Let the CSV and the page disagree about filters, or export unbounded result sets
Rename the transaction association to something that clashes with ActiveRecord, or expose raw integer ids in the UI
Forget the navigation registration/consistency test or the permission check for the new page

scenarios.name: Review photos and the rating breakdown stay honest and in order
scenarios.description: PRD-20260916-catalog-batch-f1-reviews (评论系统升级一期, §十一 of the catalog upgrade plan): the store review list answered with a bare array and no paging, so a long list could only show one slice, and the storefront computed the star breakdown from that same slice — a breakdown that disagreed with the average right above it. F-1 serves the list through the standard v3 envelope with server-side paging and a server-computed distribution, and lets a signed-in customer attach up to three photos that stay private until the review itself is approved.
mustDo: Answer the list with the standard v3 envelope and a deterministic order (created_at desc, id desc) so consecutive pages neither repeat nor skip a review
Compute rating_distribution server-side, in the same meta payload and from the same scope as the returned page, so breakdown and average can never disagree
Keep pending reviews and their photos invisible: only approved reviews are listed, and their image_urls are absolute public URLs — never raw storage paths

Enforce the photo rules on the server (at most 3, jpeg/png/webp, 5 MB) and reject foreign or cancelled signed ids with the documented error codes (422 review_image_limit_exceeded / review_image_not_owned / review_image_invalid)
Tie a direct-upload blob to the customer who created it, and accept only ids that customer uploaded and has not already attached
Keep the storefront a thin client: it renders the server numbers and only uses the image limits for a fast pre-flight, and the back office shows the same photos
mustNotDo: Change the moderation lifecycle (approved stays the gate) or auto-approve a review because it carries photos
Expose raw storage paths, pending photos, or another customer's uploads, or return a bare array where the envelope belongs
Break the existing create contract (rating/title/body) or allow an unbounded number of images
Mutate or delete an existing review when a photo upload fails, or let a photo be attached by an unauthenticated request
Recompute the rating distribution in the browser from only the page currently loaded

scenarios.name: A provider settlement report becomes a ledger a person can reconcile
scenarios.description: PRD-20260916-payments-d13b-payout-ledger (slice 2 of §78-D13 / §70.2 of the payment plan): the payment stack could already reconcile local money against the provider, but the provider's own settlement batches — reference, fees, net, arrival date — had nowhere to land, so 'reconcile at end of day' only had one side. This slice imports the settlement CSV into a payout ledger, matches every line against local payments and refunds, and pushes the lines that do not line up into the difference queue from slice 1.
mustDo: Keep the ledger a record, not a money path: importing, matching and queueing write only payout rows, case rows and audit entries — never payments, refunds, transactions, the ledger, orders or stock, and never call the provider

Make importing idempotent on both levels — one payout per (store, provider, reference) and one line per (payout, provider_reference, kind) — so re-importing the same report skips instead of duplicating
Collect row-level rejections and keep going, but refuse a missing column, an empty report or an oversized upload without writing anything
Derive the payout status from its lines in one place: difference when any line is unmatched or mismatched, settled when clean and an arrival date exists, otherwise in transit

Match with one documented anchor order (charge by payment response code then session external id, refund by refund transaction id, provider-side fees and adjustments accepted as-is) and compare amounts within a one-cent tolerance, recording the delta when it is wider
Route every difference line into the reconciliation queue with a deterministic key, auto-close it when the line matches again, and never overwrite a verdict a person already gave
Show the ledger with the same filters the totals use, and provide a reason-required, audited rematch action plus import feedback that reports payouts, new lines, skipped lines and rejected rows
mustNotDo: Move money, change payment or refund state, or repair a transaction from the import or the match action
Let an amount mismatch pass silently, or treat an unknown provider reference as matched
Duplicate a payout or a line when the same report arrives twice, or keep stale difference cases after a line recovers
Reuse the generic import framework where its column-mapping staging would add a second idempotency layer on top of the ledger keys
Forget the permission check, the navigation registration/consistency test, or the balance between what the page shows and what the totals add up

scenarios.name: Scarcity is expressed as a bucket, never as a stock count
scenarios.description: PRD-20260916-catalog-batch-f2-stock-shipping (§十一 of the catalog upgrade plan): the PDP only knew in_stock / out_of_stock, so a merchant could either say nothing about urgency or expose the exact on-hand count to shoppers and scrapers — and the storefront had no shipping window or free-shipping hint at all, even though ShippingMethod already carried transit days. F-2 buckets availability for shoppers, publishes a shipping estimate read model for the PDP, and shows a scarcity badge on product cards.
mustDo: Derive the bucket from the very same availability object the existing booleans use (Stock::Quantifier), so stock_status can never contradict in_stock/purchasable
Treat untracked inventory as unlimited (in_stock) — never invent scarcity, and never claim a sale is impossible when the store does not track stock
Normalize an invalid low-stock threshold back to the documented default instead of silently bucketing everything as scarce or everything as plenty
Keep the contract additive: existing keys stay in the response and the shipping fields are optional additions old callers can ignore
Answer the shipping estimate as advice only — no rate, shipment, order or checkout state is written, and the authoritative cost is still computed at submit
Publish the transit-day assumption (weekdays, no holiday calendar) next to the numbers so the storefront cannot promise more than the merchant configured
Preload what the bucket needs so a product list costs a constant number of queries regardless of page size
mustNotDo: Publish an exact quantity (count_on_hand / total_on_hand) in any shopper-facing response, in the UI, or in structured data
Break the 4.2 availability contract or let the badge disagree with the buy button
Show a delivery window for a digital good, or claim 'no delivery' when the answer is merely unknown
Charge, reserve, move stock or write money from the estimate endpoint
Add a query per product when serializing a list because each product's bucket was computed on its own

scenarios.name: A large refund waits for a second person, and a repeated request never pays twice
scenarios.description: PRD-20260916-payments-d14-refund-approval (slice 1 of §78-D14 / §71.1 of the payment plan): a staff refund had no amount ceiling and no second pair of eyes — one mistaken click moved money. This slice puts a policy gate in front of the human entry point: at or below the store limit the refund executes as before, above it the refund is stored durably but held until a different person approves it; a rejected hold cancels the request and releases the refundable amount, and a repeated submission with the same request key reuses the first refund instead of paying twice.
mustDo: Keep the gate at the human entry point only: the orchestrator and provider gateway paths inside Refunds::Request must stay unattended, so cancelling an order never hangs on an approval

Store the policy on the store, normalise it conservatively, and never read it with side effects: an unusable limit means everything needs approval rather than nothing does, and a switched-off policy reproduces exactly today's behaviour
Hold above the limit as a durable requested refund that is not enqueued, plus one pending approval row carrying a snapshot of the rule it was held under
Enforce separation of duties in the service, not only in the view: the approver must exist and must differ from the requester, so nobody approves or rejects their own request
Make approval the only moment execution is enqueued, and keep repeated approvals idempotent so a double click cannot queue two executions
Require a reason to reject, cancel only a request that has not yet reached the provider, and release the refundable amount by moving it to canceled

Make a repeated submission with the same request key return the first refund, with a unique index as the concurrency backstop, and audit every path (auto, requested, approved, rejected, policy updated)
mustNotDo: Call the provider, write money logs, or change payment or order amounts from the gate, the approval or the rejection — execution stays with the existing job
Let a policy that cannot be parsed silently auto-approve, or let an unknown currency scope disable a limit that should apply
Allow the requester to approve their own refund through the API, the back office, or a direct service call
Queue a second execution for an already-approved approval, or reject an approval that was already approved
Create a second refund for the same request key, or expose raw integer ids in the new admin API contract field

scenarios.name: Bulk moderation is the single-row action applied N times
scenarios.description: PRD-20260916-catalog-batch-f3-review-bulk-moderation (§十 of the catalog upgrade plan, the leftover "Admin Bulk Approve / Reject"): moderating reviews was one click per row, so a post-promotion queue of eighty pending reviews meant eighty clicks. The generic B-1 bulk framework already existed (confirm modal + table registration) but the reviews worklist had never been wired to it. F-3 registers the two actions and executes them row by row — never as one status update.
mustDo: Transition every selected review through the same state machine the single-row action uses, so side effects and the audit trail stay identical
Authorize each review individually and report the ones the operator may not touch instead of failing the whole batch
Report per-outcome counts (updated / unauthorized / state not allowed / not found) and never roll back rows that already moved
Refuse an empty selection, an unknown action, and anything above the documented per-request cap
Reuse the existing bulk-action registration and confirm modal instead of inventing a second interaction pattern
Keep the public contract untouched: only approved reviews are visible, the rating aggregate still counts approved rows only, and no Store API field changes
mustNotDo: Update the status column directly (update_all / update_columns) and thereby skip state-machine side effects
Widen authorization because the operation is bulk, or let an unauthorized operator change any row
Report success when nothing changed, or leave the operator unable to tell why a row was skipped
Delete reviews in bulk (deletion stays a deliberate single-row action)
Turn the batch into one long transaction that rolls back rows already moderated

scenarios.name: Deadline tiers: warn before the window closes, then let policy decide
scenarios.description: PRD-20260916-payments-d14b-dispute-deadlines (slice 2 of the D14 payments batch): the dispute deadline sweep warned once inside a 72h window and then went quiet, so an operator who ignored that one alert silently lost the dispute. This slice turns the warning into a per-tier, idempotent ledger (T-3 / T-1 / overdue), publishes a tier event only when a new tier is first recorded, and adds a policy-gated overdue action that can mark the dispute lost when no evidence was submitted. Default policy is off, so behaviour stays identical until a store opts in.
mustDo: Compute tiers from one policy value object (default T-3 / T-1) and expose that same calculation to the service, the admin board counts, the list column and the row badge

Record each reached tier exactly once in an append-only ledger keyed by (dispute, tier); when the first scan already skipped past several tiers, backfill the ledger rows but only alert on the newest tier
Publish the tier event only for newly recorded tiers, and keep the legacy due-soon / overdue event names and payloads working

Gate the overdue auto-lose behind an explicit store policy that is off by default, cap the number of rows it can touch per run, and skip disputes that already submitted evidence, are in a provider-decided state, or are terminal
Reuse the existing state machine and audit trail when auto-losing, and keep the operator-visible reason from being overwritten
Surface counts, a filter and the reminder history in the admin console so the numbers on the board and the filtered list cannot disagree
Keep the sweep idempotent: running it twice records no duplicate ledger rows, publishes no duplicate tier event and loses no additional dispute
mustNotDo: Touch money, funds timestamps, payments, refunds, the ledger or orders, or call the provider, from the deadline path
Auto-lose a dispute that already submitted evidence, is terminal, or whose store policy is off, or exceed the per-run cap
Write a second ledger row for a tier already recorded, or re-alert for a backfilled tier
Apply one store's deadline policy, ledger rows or auto-lose action to another store's disputes when the sweep is scoped to a single store
Change the existing due-soon / overdue event names or payloads, or break the existing scan semantics
Mix in the provider-side deadline verification, external reminder channels or the chargeback-rate board reserved for the next slice

scenarios.name: Ordering a paged list never repeats or skips a row
scenarios.description: PRD-20260916-catalog-batch-f4-review-sorting (§十 of the catalog upgrade plan): the store review list was locked to newest-first, so on a product with hundreds of reviews the lowest ratings — the ones a shopper actually wants before buying — could only be reached by paging through everything. F-4 turns the hardcoded order into a whitelisted parameter and gives the PDP a sorting control, without touching the pagination envelope, the rating distribution or the approved-only rule.
mustDo: Whitelist the orderings and fall back to the default for unknown or blank values rather than surfacing internal values through error codes
End every ordering with a unique tie-break so a paged walk over rows that share a rating and a timestamp neither repeats nor skips them
Echo the ordering that was actually applied in the response metadata, keeping every pre-existing metadata key intact
Keep the aggregate (distribution, average, count) computed over the whole approved population so it is identical under every ordering and on every page
Refetch the first page when the shopper changes the ordering instead of merging a new order into already-appended pages, and keep the visible list when that refetch fails
Leave the default path behaviourally identical to the pre-change release
mustNotDo: Accept an arbitrary order string (SQL-level ordering from user input) or return a 4xx that reveals the allowed values
Sort by a column that is not unique without a tie-break, or recompute the aggregate from the current page
Let a new ordering mix with pages fetched under the old one, or collapse the list when a refetch fails
Change which records are public (only approved) or alter the pagination contract's existing keys
Ship the control without localized labels for every supported locale

scenarios.name: Generated types and their tests ship with the change, and a temp-index commit leaves the shared index honest
scenarios.description: Catalog batch F-0 (cleanup of F-1/F-2 leftovers, 2026-09-16): the review image fields and the stock bucket reached the contract and the platform SDK, but the backend-side Typelizer outputs, the two component test files and one PRD status line were never committed — so CI kept running an older type surface and never ran those tests. The same window exposed a second hazard: committing through a temporary index left the real index holding the previous HEAD's tree, which renders in `git status` as a fabricated revert of the whole batch and would be carried into anyone's next pathless `git commit`.
mustDo: After a serializer/contract change, run the generation chain and commit every output it owns (backend typelizer types, backend SDK mirrors, platform copies) so `generated:check` is green on a clean checkout, not only locally
Commit a component's test file in the same change as the component, so CI actually executes it instead of silently reporting a smaller suite
Verify the shipped type surface really contains the new fields (e.g. image_urls, stock_status) in every mirror rather than assuming the sync step covered it
When committing through a temporary index, restore the shared index to the new HEAD afterwards and confirm `git status` shows only intended work-in-progress
Re-run the docs/knowledge sync gate before pushing and satisfy it in the same PR: component change to skill, skill change to scenario library, PRD status to index
mustNotDo: Leave generated artifacts or untracked test files behind for a later batch, or rely on a locally generated file that was never committed
Hand-edit a generated type file to make a check pass instead of re-running generation
Leave the shared index holding a tree older than HEAD, where any pathless commit becomes an accidental revert of shipped work
Close a batch while a knowledge gate is unsatisfied, or claim verification from a test run that CI never performed

scenarios.name: Social proof only comes from real, revocable, one-per-person votes
scenarios.description: Catalog batch F-5 (PRD-20260916-catalog-batch-f5-helpful-vote, §十 of the catalog upgrade plan): a shopper could not tell the storefront that a review helped, so there was no signal to surface the long useful review and no way to order by usefulness. F-5 adds attributed votes (one per customer per review, revocable), a public count, a `most_helpful` ordering, and a merchant-facing column — without ever exposing who voted, without letting anyone vote on their own review, and without letting a vote be spent twice.
mustDo: Put the uniqueness guarantee in the database (unique index on review + voter) and treat the model validation as a friendly error only — a double click or a retried request must never inflate the count
Answer voting calls with the authoritative state (count plus whether this caller's vote is recorded) so the caller never has to guess whether the write landed
Attribute every vote to a signed-in customer while keeping the public surface aggregate-only: a count plus the caller's own state — never a voter id, name or list
Answer `null` (not `false`) when the caller's own state is unknown (anonymous reads), so 'not asked' is not reported as 'decided against'
Restrict votes to what the reader can actually see (approved reviews in the caller's store) and refuse self-votes with a stable, documented error code
Make the count a counter cache so a list page reads it per row instead of issuing a query per review
Extend the existing ordering whitelist (stable tie-break included) rather than adding a second sorting mechanism, and keep the fallback and metadata contract unchanged

Ship the client side through the repo's own gates: a vote UI that fails the formatter/linter (`pnpm check`) or a storefront build blocks the release, and touching the SDK client means rebuilding and committing the published `dist` (hash-named type chunks included)

Keep the component independent of route context it does not own: prefer deriving the bits it needs from data it already reads (e.g. the pathname) over hooks that every caller — pages and their tests — would have to provide
mustNotDo: Let the same customer vote twice, or let the UI show a vote the API did not confirm
Expose who voted, or turn the vote into an unattributable counter that cannot support abuse review
Allow voting on your own review, on a pending/rejected review, or across stores
Ship the ordering without a unique tie-break, or compute the aggregate from the current page
Move money, stock or moderation state from a vote, or promise ranking guarantees the data cannot support
Hand-edit generated artifacts (or leave the SDK `dist` referencing a type chunk that was never committed) to get a check to pass

scenarios.name: A risk list is a registry until a person says otherwise
scenarios.description: PRD-20260916-payments-d15-risk-lists (slice 1 of the D15 risk batch, business plan 搂72.3): fraud operations had no way to record the emails, IPs, BINs or card fingerprints behind a run of bad orders, and no audit of what they knew and when. This slice adds the list registry (denylist / allowlist, per store or global, with expiry and revocation), bulk CSV import/export, and an assessment ledger that turns a list hit into a recorded decision 鈥?feeding the approval loop the platform already had, without blocking, refunding or capturing anything.
mustDo: Normalise the subject value before storing it and key the row on that normalised identity, so the same subject never becomes two rows and the same CSV can be imported twice
Keep expired and revoked entries visible for auditing while making them stop matching, and never physically delete a list row
Let an allowlist entry short-circuit a denylist hit, and default a denylist hit to needs-review instead of blocking
Record one assessment per decision with the matched entries, the subject data used and the evaluated time, so an operator can explain why an order was flagged
Reuse the existing considered-risky flag and approval path when a decision is not allow, and never re-flag an order that was already approved
Scope matching to the order's own store plus global entries, and keep CSV export and the workbench reading the same filtered scope
Mask every subject value in the UI and in audit payloads, and keep the raw value only in the permission-gated CSV export
mustNotDo: Block, cancel or refund an order, change payment or order state, move money or call the provider from the list or assessment path
Apply one store's list to another store's orders, or let a store edit a global row by accident
Store the same subject twice because it was typed with different casing, spacing or separators, or fail the whole import because one row is invalid
Leak raw emails, IPs, BINs or fingerprints into the workbench, the order page, the audit trail or the logs
Turn a list hit straight into an irreversible action 鈥?the 3DS policy, rule engine versions and review queue are later slices

scenarios.name: Merging duplicates moves references, never rewrites history
scenarios.description: Catalog batch D-3 (PRD-20260916-catalog-d3-product-merge, §十二 of the catalog upgrade plan): duplicate detection could find the same product twice but offered no way to put it back together — fixing that by hand meant retyping SKUs, losing reviews and breaking old URLs. D-3 merges one product into another: movable references move, the old URL gets a 301, the merged-away product is archived and soft-deleted with a trace, and the whole thing can be undone — while historical orders keep pointing exactly where they pointed before.
mustDo: Keep the preview strictly read-only and let execution reuse the very same impact calculation, so what the merchant was shown cannot differ from what runs
Close the accounting: every moved record is recorded per id in a ledger row, and moved + skipped always equals what the preview counted
Skip conflicts instead of overwriting (SKU already on the survivor, customer already reviewed the survivor) and report each skipped item with its reason, leaving the record where it was
Never rewrite history: line items, orders, payments and transaction rows must be byte-identical before and after the merge — and after the undo
Preserve every skipped or un-migrated record: soft-delete the absorbed product without triggering dependent destruction, and stamp it with a trace of where it went
Make the merge reversible from the ledger alone, restoring each recorded item, the previous state and the redirect, and refuse the whole undo when any recorded item is gone or moved elsewhere
Keep the operation idempotent and store-scoped: repeating a merge or an undo changes nothing, and a product from another store is never touched
mustNotDo: Write anything during the preview, or let the preview and the execution disagree about what will move
Delete records to make the merge simpler, or silently overwrite a conflicting variant/review
Re-point orders, payments or ledger rows at a different product to 'tidy up' history
Perform a partial undo, or undo something the ledger did not record
Leave the merchant without a reversal path, or require them to reconstruct what happened from logs
